title: Pinning compatibility schema and onboarding policy for model versions
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Goal: Define a machine-readable compatibility schema and an operational onboarding policy for 'pinned' model versions so that customers can rely on stable prompt/response behavior and predictable performance when they pin a model in the Redwood Catalog. This ticket delivers: 1) a compatibility schema that specifies the contract surface (prompt tokenization, canonical prompt shapes, required function-call contracts, output JSON schemas, and supported runtime parameters), 2) a publisher process for a performance profile artifact (latency percentiles, throughput under representative batch shapes, memory/KV cache usage, and quantization metadata), and 3) CI + runtime enforcement rules that prevent incompatible model variants from being accepted as a pinned target without explicit migration steps and sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable compatibility schema (JSON Schema) that covers: tokenizer id/version, canonical prompt labels and expected placeholders, required function output keys and types, supported runtime params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequence semantics) and a backwards-compatibility level enum (STRICT, STABLE, COMPATIBLE)
A documented onboarding checklist for model owners that includes: sample golden prompts, suggested unit/regression tests, perf benchmark scripts, and upgrade notes for non-backward compatible changes
Automated CI checks that validate a candidate model artifact against the compatibility schema and run the provided golden prompts; failures surface as blocking errors in the onboarding PR

A published performance profile artifact for each pinned version stored in model-catalog (JSON blob) with fields: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec for 1/8/32 batch shapes, peak GPU memory, KV cache working set size, and quantization flags

Runtime enforcement: when a customer pins a model version, the control plane validates the model artifact exists and the compatibility level is >= STABLE or the customer explicitly acknowledges risks; incompatible pin attempts are rejected with actionable error messages

Backward compatibility policy documented with examples of allowed patch changes vs forbidden changes (e.g., small weight-only optimizations that preserve tokenizer and output schema allowed; changes to tokenizer or function contract require a new major pinned version and migration guide)
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating a pinned model serving the same set of golden prompts with token-level diff thresholds and a performance delta budget; test added to nightly regression suite
tasks: Draft JSON Schema for compatibility contract and share for review (Eng + PM + Docs)
Extend model registry to accept and store 'compatibility' and 'performance_profile' artifacts
Create onboarding checklist template in Confluence and link sample golden prompts
Implement CI plugin that runs schema validation and golden-prompt regression; wire into model build pipeline
Implement control plane validation for pin requests and user-facing error messages
Add perf benchmark harness and standard batch shapes; publish perf JSON to model-catalog on successful benchmark
Write migration guidance for tokenizer/IO changes and review with Applied ML
Add e2e nightly test that validates pinned-version contract and perf budgets
risks: Overly strict schema will block legitimate model performance optimizations and increase onboarding friction
Inconsistent tokenization across toolchains could produce silent behavior changes for pinned versions
Perf profiling noise: hardware variability may make perf profiles brittle unless we standardize runners
Customer confusion if pinging semantics differ across hosted/dedicated/private deployments
notes: Proposed compatibility levels: STRICT (no change permitted to tokenizer or output schema), STABLE (semantic output preserved; minor nondeterministic token-level diffs tolerated up to configurable threshold), COMPATIBLE (best-effort; caller must opt-in). We should include example JSON Schema fragments in the first review: function_call.name required; function_call.args schema required for any declared function; top-level 'response_format' property describing expected JSON structure. Coordinate with Applied ML on tokenizer id/version tagging. Perf profile publishing will be implemented as a simple JSON blob versioned alongside the model artifact.
